problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(-2i-8j)\,\text{m/s},$ and when $t=4\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $2i\,\text{m/s}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.

feedback.problem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. When $t=0\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(i-6j)\,\text{m/s},$ and when $t=3\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle is $(4i+3j)\,\text{m/s}.$ Calculate the acceleration of the particle.
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
u=i-6j,\,v=4i+3j,\,t=3,
$$

into the equation above, we can solve for $a,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 4i+3j & =(i-6j)+a(3) \\ 3i+9j & =3a \\ a & =\frac{1}{3}(3i+9j) \\  & =(i+3j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
